headline: Broad-based growth beats outlook; full-year guidance raised
summary_short: RB Global reported second-quarter revenue of $1,317.1 million (+11.1% y/y) on 11% GTV growth to $4.7 billion, with net income of $143.5 million (+30.7% y/y) and diluted EPS of $0.71 (+34.0% y/y); the company raised full-year GTV and Adjusted EBITDA guidance.
summary_long: GTV grew 11% y/y to $4.7 billion on strong Automotive volumes and acquisition contributions (including BigIron); ex-acquisitions, GTV rose 7%. Service revenue rose 5% as higher GTV was offset by a 110bp take-rate decline from acquisition mix and auto pricing incentives. Inventory sales revenue jumped 28% on HE&T contract-preference shifts and acquisitions. Net income rose 31% y/y to $143.6 million on higher operating income and lower interest expense, partly offset by higher taxes. RB Global raised full-year GTV growth guidance to 9%-11% (from 6%-9%) and Adjusted EBITDA to $1,495-$1,545 million (from $1,485-$1,545 million); tax-rate and capex guidance held. Cash fell to $524.9 million after acquisition spending, buybacks, and dividends, partly offset by debt issuance; long-term debt rose to $2,885.6 million.

drivers.explanation: CEO cited durable marketplace growth and the BigIron acquisition strengthening the company's US agriculture position; CFO cited Automotive growth, acquisition contributions, and cost discipline as drivers of the quarter's earnings growth.
Total revenue rose on 11% GTV growth from Automotive volume and share gains plus acquisitions, and a 28% jump in inventory sales revenue tied to HE&T contract-preference shifts.
Net income available to common stockholders rose mainly on higher operating income and lower interest expense, partly offset by higher income tax expense.
Diluted EPS tracked the 31% rise in net income available to common stockholders, since diluted weighted-average shares outstanding were roughly flat y/y (186.9M vs 186.6M).
Six-month cash flow shows the decline driven by $331.1M of acquisition spending, $150.0M of share buybacks, and $132.8M of dividends paid, partly offset by $456.4M of new long-term debt issuance.
Six-month cash flow shows $456.4M of new long-term debt issuance against $166.7M of repayments, with proceeds funding acquisitions and buybacks alongside operating cash flow.
